findings.title: The new capability's description still names the retired requirement
findings.recommendation: The Capabilities line for orbit-program-brief lists 'what a brief rendered before the archive record says', the wording of the requirement the walk replaced with 'A brief says only what the archive recorded', which now covers every archive state, not only the time before the record. walk_entry.title: An archived change with no archive record gets the pre-archive rows, which then say false things

commentary: A verification of the two walks, graded entry by entry against the files each claims, then the nine passes over the union of their scopes and the residual list from the commit that added codex's return (six files, every one inside some entry's edit record). The walk's large edits held: the second requirement's rewrite carries all four archive states with a scenario each, the snapshot paragraph and its after-the-save scenario, the term rule with two scenarios, and the output details the golden renders will fix; validate --strict passes. The misses are both residue of one supersession — D-br-6 replacing D-br-4 — at two sites the cascade did not search: the live D-br-3 mechanism entry in explore.md and the proposal's one-line capability description. Neither changes what apply builds; both are pointer and wording repairs. Not re-checked here: the propose-time ledger entry that recorded the single 'not yet synced' label still reads as current in its chain; the walk's new entry for decision A records the reversed call beside it, which is how the records model a changed call.
